text:
rowan: heads up: ci backup job leaked KMS-wrapped ciphertexts into the build logs during a retention-run. tiny volume but sensitive. snippet below. tagging sec.

rowan: ```
2025-09-10T07:12:03Z INFO backup-job: snapshot write id=snap-20250910 wrap_ct=Cr2...
2025-09-10T07:12:04Z INFO backup-job: snapshot write id=snap-20250910-2 wrap_ct=Cr2...
```

jess: yikes. which key and who had access?

omar: Key: projects/redwood-prod/locations/global/keyRings/backups/cryptoKeys/snapshot-wrap (v1). The CI runner service account ci-runner@redwood-ci.iam.gserviceaccount.com had encrypter perms via a broad project-level binding for onboarding.

security-bot: IAM ALERT: serviceAccount:ci-runner@redwood-ci.iam.gserviceaccount.com performed cloudkms.encrypt on snapshot-wrap at 2025-09-10T07:12:04Z.

vaultd: Vault audit for namespace "backups" shows multiple write events around 07:11-07:13. retention currently 30d. recommend increasing to 180d for post-incident forensics.

jess: immediate actions proposal:
- revoke encrypter grant for ci-runner now (omar)
- create new wrap key snapshot-wrap-rot1 and implement a short lived grant model (grant tokens) for runners (security)
- generate hitlist from storage + build logs, export to secure GCS path and lock access (rowan)
- enable dual-decrypt support in restore flow for 48h to avoid downtime (omar)
- run batched re-encrypt (rewrap) task with verify checksums (jess)
- add admission + CI guardrail to forbid printing wrap_ct values (k8s-policy-bot + ci team)
- bump Vault audit retention for backups to 180d and add alert: encrypt_calls_by_sa > 2/min => page.

omar: I'll remove the binding and push a terraform change to replace the wide encrypter with a limited ephemeral grant. snippet to remove binding: 

omar: ```hcl
resource "google_project_iam_member" "rm_ci_encrypter" {
  project = var.project_id
  role    = "roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter"
  member  = "serviceAccount:ci-runner@redwood-ci.iam.gserviceaccount.com"
}
# follow-up: create a grant using KMS grant tokens for ephemeral encrypt rights
```

jess: For rewrap I'll author a small re-encryptor service that pulls the hitlist and does verified rewraps in batches of 250. plan: dry-run in staging -> canary 250 -> ramp. CLI: 

jess: ```bash
python tools/reencrypt.py \
  --hitlist gs://redwood-sec/exports/backup-hitlist-20250910.json \
  --src-key projects/redwood-prod/.../snapshot-wrap \
  --dst-key projects/redwood-prod/.../snapshot-wrap-rot1 \
  --batch 250 --verify --dry-run
```

rowan: I'll produce the hitlist from build logs + storage change history and put it under gs://redwood-sec/incident-3755554321/hitlist.json (ACL: infra-sec-only).

k8s-policy-bot: Creating policy: deny logging of fields matching regex "wrap_ct=\\w+" in containers running in backups namespaces. PR: https://git.redwood.internal/policies/logging/pull/812

security-bot: Ticket created SEC-2300 "CI backup logs exposed KMS wrapped ciphertexts: rewrap + ephemeral grants + logging guardrails". Assignees: jess, omar, rowan. Priority: P1.

sre-oncall: I'll schedule a brief deploy freeze for backup jobs and coordinate staging dry-run -> prod canary windows. ETA 40m. Abort thresholds: >0.3% restore failure or >2x CPU during rewrap.

amar: (note) After rewrap completes we should rotate any long-lived tokens that could reference affected snapshots: CI tokens, backup service principals, and any external partner connectors. Also schedule a 72h hold before retiring old key versions and run a cross-check sweep.

omar: Implementing ephemeral grant model: will use KMS IAM grants + short-lived grant tokens that expire after 1h. This reduces blast radius compared to project-level binding. I'll post TF + helper scripts.

jess: Running staging dry-run now. Will post the summary: number of blobs in hitlist, any checksum mismatches, and estimated prod duration.

rowan: I'll also add a short onboarding doc update: CI jobs must not log ciphertexts and must use the KMS grant helper for encrypt operations. We should add a linter to catch suspicious log lines in CI.

security-bot: Reminder: attach hitlist and staging logs to SEC-2300 and mark as "in-progress".

omar: Done revoking binding. Pushing TF change and starting roll of ephemeral grants tooling.

jess: Dry-run results: 42 blobs in staging hitlist, dry-run rewrap succeeded with 0 mismatches. planning prod canary in 60m for 250 blobs. Will update after canary.

rowan: Good job. Keep thread updated; we'll collect post-run checklist (hitlist path, batches processed, rotated tokens list, PR links for TF + logging policy, Vault retention PR) and do a short postmortem in 48h.
